data.title: Accendra Health Receives Continued Listing Standard Notice from NYSE Regarding Market Capitalization and Stockholders’ Equity; Intends to Submit Business Plan and Return to Compliance with NYSE Listing Standard​
data.description:
Accendra Health, Inc. () (the Company) today announced that on October 27, 2026, it received a notice (the “Notice”) from the New York Stock Exchange (the “NYSE”) notifying the Company that it is not in compliance with Section 802.01B of the NYSE’s continued listing standards that the Company have an average market capitalization of not less than $50.0 million over a consecutive 30 trading-day period and stockholders’ equity of not less than $50.0 million. The Notice does not result in the immediate delisting of the Company’s Class A Common Stock (the “Common Stock”) from the NYSE.

The Company intends to respond to the NYSE within ten business days of receipt of the Notice affirming its intent to submit a business plan. Pursuant to Section 802.01B, the Company has a period of 45 calendar days following receipt of the Notice to submit a business plan that demonstrates how the Company intends to regain compliance with Section 802.01B within 18 months of receipt of the Notice. The NYSE will review the business plan and, if accepted, the Company will be subject to quarterly monitoring by the NYSE of the progress of the business plan.

​​The Company’s Common Stock will continue to be listed and trade on the NYSE during this period, subject to its compliance with other NYSE continued listing standards. The receipt of the Notice does not affect the Company’s business, operations or reporting requirements with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Safe Harbor

This release is intended to be disclosure through methods reasonably designed to provide broad, non-exclusionary distribution to the public in compliance with the SEC’s Fair Disclosure Regulation. This release contains certain “forward looking” statements made pursuant to the Safe Harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements include, but are not limited to, statements relating to the Company’s ability to maintain the listing of its Common Stock on the NYSE, its intentions regarding regaining compliance with the NYSE’s continued listing standards, including the submission and acceptance of a business plan, its ability to create shareholder value, and stock price expectations, as well as the Company’s anticipated future prospects and performance. Forward-looking statements involve known and unknown risks and uncertainties that may cause our actual results in future periods to differ materially from those projected or contemplated in the forward-looking statements. Investors should refer to the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, filed with the SEC on February 20, 2026, including the section captioned “Item 1A. Risk Factors,” as applicable, and subsequent quarterly reports on Form 10-Q and current reports on Form 8-K filed with or furnished to the SEC, for a discussion of certain known risk factors that could cause the Company’s actual results to differ materially from its current estimates. These filings are available at www.accendrahealth.com. Given these risks and uncertainties, the Company can give no assurance that any forward-looking statements will, in fact, transpire and, therefore, cautions investors not to place undue reliance on them. The Company specifically disclaims any obligation to update or revise any forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future developments or otherwise.

About Accendra Health

Accendra Health, Inc. () is a leading nationwide provider of products, technology, and services that support health beyond the hospital for millions of people each year. We connect patients, providers, and insurers, delivering innovative solutions that help promote better health outcomes and improve quality of life for people living with chronic, complex health conditions. Backed by the industry-leading expertise of our Apria and Byram brands, Accendra Health is reimagining the future of home-based care. To learn more about our broad portfolio of essentials for diabetes, sleep health, wound care, respiratory care, urology, and ostomy, visit www.accendrahealth.com.

data.title: Higher Rates Ahead? Three Fed Officials Have Called For A Gradual Uptick In Interest Rates This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan indicated support for a minimum of two additional 25-basis-point rate increases. 
  • Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin and St. Louis Fed's Alberto Musalem emphasized that incremental adjustments help businesses and households adapt smoothly. 
  • The push for tighter policy comes as inflation remains above the central bank's 2% target, accompanied by robust third-quarter economic growth driven by consumer spending and artificial intelligence investments. 

Top Federal Reserve officials signaled this week that further interest rate increases will be required to control persistent inflation, though they advocated for a measured pace of tightening to prevent unnecessary disruption to the broader economy.

The public comments from a trio of regional central bank presidents came shortly after the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged. The pause follows a September rate hike—the central bank's first rate increase since 2023.

Measured Approach 

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan stated during a speech at Davidson College that economic conditions warrant additional monetary tightening.

"It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases," Logan said. She noted that skipping a single meeting does not alter the central bank's ultimate destination and argued that a gradual approach allows households, businesses, and financial markets to adjust smoothly.

Other central bank leaders echoed the call for incremental moves. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin noted in a radio interview that a gradual path remains prudent, while St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem pointed out at a New York event that early, incremental shifts typically cause less disturbance than sudden, drastic changes later.

Financial market futures indicate investors expect the next quarter-point rate hike to occur at the Fed’s final meeting of the year in December, followed by a potential pause in January and another increase in March.

Economic Growth And Inflation Pressures

Calls for monetary tightening come amid stubborn inflation and resilient economic activity. Data released Thursday revealed that the central bank’s primary inflation metric reached 3.6% in September, boosted in part by rebounding crude oil prices. Annual inflation has now remained above the Fed's 2% target for over five years.

Concurrently, third-quarter economic growth accelerated to its fastest rate in a year. Strong consumer demand and substantial corporate investments—particularly within the burgeoning artificial intelligence sector—have buoyed overall expansion.

Barkin noted that a sustained surge in demand would be a key factor compelling policymakers to lean harder on monetary brakes.

Long-Term Outlook

While Fed Chair Kevin Warsh refrained from explicitly laying out his interest rate forecast, he reaffirmed that curbing high inflation remains the central bank's top priority while describing financial conditions as tighter during his October monetary policy speech.

Despite the majority vote to pause rate adjustments at the recent meeting, internal divergence remains. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented against the decision to hold rates constant, favoring an immediate second consecutive rate hike instead.

Logan outlined a temporary endpoint for the upcoming cycle, suggesting the Fed should pause after two more quarter-point increases to evaluate economic performance.

"The end goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive so we can sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices," Logan added.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) dropped about 1.6%, while the tech-heavy Invesco QQQ eased over 3% on Friday. While retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bullish’ for the SPY, it turned ‘bearish’ for the QQQ.

data.title: Why Intel's stock saw its worst day in decades - and a $140 billion wipeout
Reliance Retail Q2 results: Net profit falls 24% to Rs.2,611 crore; revenue rises 6%
data.description:
Mumbai/Bengaluru, Oct. 30 -- Reliance Retail Ltd's net profit fell 24.3% year-on-year to Rs.2,611 crore in the September quarter, as higher costs and a shift in the festive calendar weighed on margins. Revenue from operations, however, rose 5.8% to Rs.80,220 crore, according to an exchange filing.

On a sequential basis, net profit declined 6.9% from Rs.2,805 crore in the June quarter. The figures are adjusted for the restructuring and demerger of the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) and consumer brands business in December 2025. Reliance Retail operates across grocery, consumer electronics, fashion and lifestyle and online commerce.

"Reliance Retail had a steady quarter, with growth sustained across all formats and channels," Mukesh D. Ambani, chairman and managing director of Reliance Industries Ltd, said in a statement. "Consumer demand stayed healthy, supported by our extensive physical and digital presence and our continued focus on serving the diverse needs of Indian consumers."

The company flagged several challenges during the quarter, including inflation at a two-year high, a weaker rupee and a deficient monsoon across key agricultural states. Consumer price inflation stood at 5.5% and food inflation at 7.7% in September, adding to input, freight and packaging costs. The rupee's weakness also raised the landed cost of imported goods, particularly electronics and fashion products. Meanwhile, the monsoon deficit put further pressure on food prices and made rural demand uneven.

The festive calendar also shifted this year, with major festivals such as Navratri and Diwali falling in the third quarter, unlike last year.

Reliance Retail's Ebitda, or earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization, stood at Rs.6,228 crore before a one-time charge. Its Ebitda margin was 7.8%, down 120 basis points from a year earlier.

The company also reported a one-time impairment charge of Rs.108 crore on 7-Eleven during the quarter. The retailer had shut all its stores in India by the end of September.

Reliance Retail said its Ebitda margin reflected planned investments in digital commerce, input-cost inflation absorbed by the company, and the shift in the festive season to the third quarter.

However, average order values in its quick-commerce operations, including JioMart and Ajio Rush, increased during the quarter, while average delivery times declined substantially over the past four quarters, according to Reliance Retail chief financial officer Dinesh Taluja.

The company does not plan to raise prices to improve margins. "Prices are how the market determines where competition is. But we will sweat our assets more and leverage our scale to improve our margins," Taluja said, referring to Reliance Retail's network of 19,947 stores.

Reliance Consumer Products Ltd (RCPL) reported a 1.6-fold increase in gross revenue in the September quarter, supported by its Independence staples brand and Campa beverages business.

Gross revenue rose to Rs.8,266 crore in the three months ended September, while revenue for the first half of FY27 reached Rs.16,900 crore, about 1.8 times the year-earlier figure, according to Reliance Industries' quarterly presentation. RCPL said it had achieved about 80% of its total sales for the previous financial year in the first six months of FY27.

Daily essentials, led by Independence, generated about Rs.7,000 crore in sales in the first half, growing 1.7 times from a year earlier. Campa-led beverages recorded sales of more than Rs.5,250 crore during the same period, crossing 90% of the brand-led category's sales for the whole of FY26 in just six months, the company said.

The beverages business grew 2.1 times year-on-year. RCPL reported double-digit market share across several states as it expanded Campa's presence in domestic and overseas markets.

Campa's international expansion is gathering pace. In Australia, the brand has entered major supermarket chains. It has also launched in Kenya, adding to its presence in Ghana, Nigeria and other markets. RCPL said it had expanded its presence in the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Malaysia.

RCPL is also widening its portfolio beyond beverages and staples. Its home and personal care categories recorded strong growth following product-range extensions and a nationwide expansion, with Glimmer gaining early consumer traction.

The company has also entered the dairy category with ice creams, which it describes as an accessible premium offering.

data.title: Western Alliance Bancorporation 3Q 2026: Revenue $1.01B, EPS $2.45— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Western Alliance Bancorporation reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $1.01 billion, up 8.1% year over year, and net income attributable to the company of $270.1 million, up 6.6%. Diluted EPS rose 7.5% to $2.45, as higher net interest income and commercial banking fees more than offset lower mortgage gains.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $1.01B, compared with $938.2M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 8.1%.
  • Net income attributable to Western Alliance was $270.1M, compared with $253.4M; YoY change 6.6%.
  • Diluted EPS was $2.45, compared with $2.28; YoY change 7.5%.

Business Highlights

  • The company transitioned out approximately $3.0B of higher-cost deposits during the quarter and $4.5B cumulatively as it continued optimizing its funding mix.
  • Commercial banking fees grew 50.2% year over year, while mortgage gains declined 26.2% amid lower originations and secondary marketing revenue.
  • Held-for-investment loans increased 4.9% since year-end, with growth in commercial, hotel franchise finance and residential lending.
  • Western Alliance continued resolving problem loans, taking possession of two commercial real estate office properties and pursuing recoveries through litigation.

Original SEC Filing: WESTERN ALLIANCE BANCORPORATION [ WAL ] - 10-Q - Oct. 30, 2026

Business Highlights

  • The company remains a blank-check company seeking a target and has not selected a specific business combination.

  • New directors took office in July 2025, when Yip Tsz Yan became CEO, CFO and Board Chair; a director resigned in October 2025.
  • Nasdaq trading was suspended in September 2024, and the company’s securities are now quoted on the OTC market.
  • The company expects ongoing public-company and acquisition-search costs and aims to complete a business combination before the deadline.
